 ORDER Heard and perused the case diary.
2.

This order shall govern the disposal of these miscellaneous criminal cases as they have arisen out of same crime number of the same police station, hence, they are heard analogously and are being decided by this common order.

3 . These are first application filed by the applicants under Section 483 of BNSS (Section 439 of Cr.P.C.) for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.327/2024 dated (not mentioned), registered at Police Station-Sector -1, Pithampur, District-Dhar for the offence under Sections 420, 120-b, 464,
467, 468, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:755 2 MCRC-249-2025 469, 471, (Section 406 for applicant Sahrukh Khan) of IPC.
Applicants are in custody since 26.05.2024.
4. Allegation against the applicants is that they are involved in the aforesaid offence wherein applicants were taking vehicles on rent and thereafter sold them.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants submitted that the applicants are innocent and have falsely been implicated in the case.
As per allegation, the applicants were taking vehicles on rent and thereafter sold them.
One of the vehicle, sold by them, has been seized.
Earlier bail applications were dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to renew the prayer after completion of two months from the date of order.
In compliance of the above liberty, these applications have been filed.
Counsel for applicants assure that the applicants will not involve themselves in any crime and they will follow the condition imposed by the Court.
Applicants are in custody since 26.05.2024 more than 07 months.
Final conclusion of trial will take sufficient long time.
Hence, he prays that the applicants be released on bail.
6. Learned Govt. Advocate for the respondent - State has opposed the bail applications and prayed for their rejection.

7. Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by counsel for both the parties, custody period, nature of allegation and also the fact that final conclusion of trial shall take sufficient long time, I deem it proper to release the accused / applicants on bail.

8. It is directed that applicants be released on bail on their furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand only) each with one solvent surety each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for their regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:755 3 MCRC-249-2025 they shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

The applicants shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS, 2023.
9.

By way of abundant caution, it is further directed that the applicant shall also mark his presence before the concerned Police Station on first and third Monday of every month between 10.00 am to 12.00 noon during pendency of the trial.

entities.text: first and third Monday of every month

sentences.text: Any default in attendance in court and marking presence in the concerned police station, would result in cancellation of bail granted by this Court thereby entitling the police to take the applicants in custody immediately.

10. This order shall remain effective till the end of the trial, but in case of bail jump and breach of any of the pre-condition of bail, it shall become ineffective and cancelled without reference to this Bench.
Certified copy, as per Rules.
